To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we built and tested an EHR-driven deep learning framework to identify patients at high risk of 30 day unschedualed readmission and demonstrated that it can be used to achieve significant cost savings.

(a) a deep learning framework that uses both expert and machine features, incorporates sequential patterns and addresses the class imbalance problem, achieves higher discrimination ability and higher cost savings; (b) the framework is robust to the choice of hyperparameters; (c) the model is able to learn the importance of features and their interactions; (d) the model can learn the importance of temporal information in EHRs.
we have developed and evaluated a deep learning based framework that predicts 30 day readmission for Congestive Heart failure patients using both expert and contextual features from the EHR.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cost sensitive LSTM model with expert and machine derived feature representation, and contextual embedding of concepts in EHR, can be used to identify high risk patients and reduce readmissions.
we present a cost sensitive LSTM framework that uses both expert and machine learned features to predict readmission in CHF patients.
the model is able to predict 30-day readmission with a good balance between recall and precision and is cost effective in identifying patients at risk of unscheduled readmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cost-sensitive LSTM model with both expert and machine-derived features, and contextual embedding of medical concepts can be used to identify patients at high risk for readmission.
a cost sensitive formulation using LSTM with expert features and contextual EHR embedding can achieve high performance in readmission prediction.
the deep learning framework can be a useful tool for predicting unscheduled 30 day hospital readmission in CHF patients.
